heading: Restore discipline — proof the substrate never moved
notes: The cited historical line ranges resolve and support the stated before snapshots, scratch-copy practice, and recorded after snapshots. However, SKILL.md:386-391 says the same checks were rerun and every value was identical, while the cited after blocks omit the repository revision recorded before the sweep (Kimi note:13-16 vs :34-35; Kagi note:13-17 vs :54-56). The evidence therefore does not support that all listed values matched. Further, endpoint fingerprints establish observed final-state equality, not literal absence of every transient write; the strict 'never written' proof needs qualification or write-level evidence. This is the blocking gap.

SKILL.md:396-400 overstates scratch-free reproducibility. Kimi note §4 (:150-177) and Kagi note §7 (:210-249) list mutate_driver.py as a scratch artifact and invoke it, but give exact edit specifications rather than the driver's source or creation steps. SCORECARD.md:16 calls the earlier driver one-off, unversioned, and not in-tree. SCORECARD.md:13 records sensitivity reruns from retained scratch, not a rebuild after scratch loss. The specs aid reconstruction but do not reproduce the run as written without reimplementing the missing driver; counted as one wrong expectation.

The named citations to the Kimi/Kagi notes are line-accurate. The G-R2-1 historical claim is supported by corpus/README.md:11 and its source erratum corpus/knowledge/gates-survey-kagi.md:554-560. 'SCORECARD round-2 verification row' is underspecified (the relevant summary is SCORECARD.md:13) and supports reruns from retained scratch, not scratch-free reconstruction; no cited numeric line range itself is wrong.

Round-2 and round-3 observations are dated 2026-10-14 history, not claims about current external checkout state. SKILL.md:401-403 accurately uses G-R2-1 as a historical dirty-baseline lesson. No obsolete Git command was identified; git status, cp -p, git checkout --, and git restore remain meaningful in the stated contexts. Historical reproduction commands were not executed.

The lsp device was unavailable: read of xd://lsp returned 'No such tool'; xd://lsp/status returned 'Tool lsp has no doc topics'. No LSP status/references/definition/diagnostics were possible. Direct reads establish the citations; text search was used only to locate references, not as semantic proof.
